stem: A 5-year-old boy living with HIV, on antiretroviral therapy, is brought in by his mother, a healthcare aide, after about three weeks of cough and reduced energy. His most recent CD4 count was within a range typically not requiring additional prophylaxis by some standards, but he has not previously received cotrimoxazole. No known TB contact in the household. No prior TB treatment, no known drug-resistant contact. Chest X-ray shows a right hilar lymph node pattern suggestive of primary TB. Exam: well-appearing overall, mild right-sided crackles, no respiratory distress.

patient.occupation: not applicable (household occupational context: mother works as a healthcare aide)
patient.social_history: Lives with mother; living with HIV, on ART, followed at a pediatric clinic
patient.exam_findings: Well-appearing overall, mild right-sided crackles, no respiratory distress, right hilar lymphadenopathy on imaging
patient.prior_treatment: On established antiretroviral therapy; no prior TB treatment; not previously on cotrimoxazole

distractors: His CD4 count treated as a reason cotrimoxazole is unnecessary, without considering that his active TB diagnosis itself changes the recommendation
Intermittent cough attributed to a string of ordinary childhood illnesses rather than a persistent process warranting focused evaluation
ntep_correct_actions: Give cotrimoxazole preventive therapy to this patient regardless of his CD4 count, since he is HIV-positive with active TB.
Perform rifampicin-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen regardless of prior treatment history, birth/residence history, contact history, or HIV status.

Perform rifampicin-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen regardless of prior treatment history, birth/residence history, contact history, or HIV status.
us_correct_actions: Base the decision to start cotrimoxazole primarily on whether this patient's CD4 count is below 200 cells/uL, since this framework reserves cotrimoxazole mainly for that group rather than using it universally.

Order rapid rifampicin-resistance testing for this patient because his HIV-positive status independently meets one of the specific risk criteria this framework uses to decide who receives testing -- not because testing is a universal policy.
critical_error_conditions: Omitting rifampicin-resistance testing for this patient despite his established TB diagnosis
expected_divergence_points: Whether cotrimoxazole preventive therapy is given to all HIV-positive TB patients regardless of CD4 count or reserved for those with CD4 below 200 cells/uL
Whether rifampicin-resistance testing is performed as a matter of universal policy or because specific risk criteria (in this case, his HIV status) are met
